text:
Alex: ran a quick nsys on prod-image v2.3.1 with a 30s steady-state feed; top kernel is surprising — not the attention kernel we expected.
Sam: can you paste the top-of-trace summary?
Alex: sure, gist of the summary:
```
nsys summary: total_runtime 29.7s
Top kernels by inclusive time:
  gpt_attn_prefetch         9.8s  (33%)
  kv_lookup_dispatch        6.1s  (20%)
  softmax_dropout_fwd       3.0s  (10%)
  gelu_fwd                  2.4s  (8%)
  layernorm_fwd             1.7s  (5%)
```
Note: gpt_attn_prefetch here is a fused prefetch+attn kernel we thought would be cheaper per token.
Maria: :thinking: that prefetch being 33% is odd — earlier traces had it ~12-15%.
Jin: any input-shape shift? small batch or shorter seqs can make prefetch overhead dominate.
Alex: input distro is skewed towards many short sequences (avg 18 tokens) after the batching heuristic change last week.
Sam: that matches — batching heuristic went from pack_until_full to cut_at_32_tokens for latency consistency.
Maria: kv_lookup_dispatch also high; looks like KV cache misses are causing back-to-back prefetch calls.
PerfBot: nsys trace uploaded to https://perf.internal/trace/3326007777 (annotated with nvtx ranges)
Sam: can we see a perfetto timeline slice for a 200ms window where the spike happens?
Alex: uploaded a small perfetto slice. Key observation: gpt_attn_prefetch launches many small kernels with low occupancy (20-30%) and frequent synchronization points.
Maria: low occupancy + many launches = SM underutilization. If kv_lookup interleaves stalls, it explains the cumulative time.
Jin: hypothesis: our batching heuristic creates more micro-batches which disables streaming prefetch path and forces fused prefetch to run per micro-batch.
Alex: also noticed a perf regression at commit abc1234 (merge: batching heuristics tweak). Prior to that, gpt_attn_prefetch was split across fewer launches with higher occupancy.
Sam: plan: 1) reproduce with nvprof sampling focused on kernel occupancy and warp efficiency; 2) instrument KV path with NVTX around kv_cache hit/miss; 3) try reverting packing threshold to pre-change for a canary.
Maria: quick instrumentation snippet to add around kv lookup:
```
NVTX_RANGE_PUSH("kv_lookup_start");
auto hit = kv_cache.get(key);
NVTX_RANGE_POP();
```
Jin: also try a temporary heuristic: if avg_seq_len < 24, use pack_until_full for 50% of requests to amortize prefetch.
Alex: expected delta? rough estimate 7-12% p50 latency improvement if prefetch time drops and occupancy increases.
Sam: I'll run nvprof with `--metrics achieved_occupancy,sm_efficiency,warp_efficiency` against a replayed traffic sample and push results here by EOD.
Maria: if confirmed, we should adjust kernel-selection thresholds too — choose the non-prefetch attention kernel when micro-batch rate > X.
Alex: agree. Jin — can you draft the canary rollout plan for the heuristic tweak (5% traffic -> 25% -> 100%) with automatic rollback if p95 regresses > 5%?
Jin: on it, will include perf triggers and NVTX tagging for easier rollup.
Alex: thanks team. Sam, assign yourself the nvprof run and post results. If we see occupancy improvement, we'll prioritize a revert/soft-toggle.
Sam: assigned, starting run now. Will report back in this thread. :thumbsup:
